quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker's reaction is whenever they enter the room.
quests.explanation: Smiling automatically at the finished room shows lasting happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: We painted the whole room this weekend. Now every time I walk in, I can't help smiling.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Ask whether anyone is being blamed, or whether something was simply lost.
quests.explanation: Nobody is blamed and nothing can be done, so the feeling is sadness about the loss rather than anger.
quests.textToSpeak: My ice cream fell on the ground before I even tasted it.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice the question at the end and how it is asked.
quests.explanation: The sharp rhetorical question shows the speaker feels let down and is upset with him. Anger is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: He promised to help me move, and now he says he's busy? Are you kidding me?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker asks for just before the performance.
quests.explanation: Asking for a hand to hold before going on stage shows nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: The music is starting, and it's almost our turn to walk on stage. Somebody hold my hand.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice the word 'finally' and the time the speaker has been waiting.
quests.explanation: Two years of waiting ends tomorrow, and the speaker sounds eager. That's what the clues add up to: excitement.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been saving for two years, and tomorrow I finally pick up my very first bicycle!

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the question the speaker asks about what they see.
quests.explanation: The speaker didn't know about any of this and asks what is going on. That's surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a cake on my desk, and balloons, and everyone is shouting my name. What is this?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to how the speaker ends the sentence.
quests.explanation: Noticing a pattern and asking what's inside shows a wish to find out. That's what the clues add up to: curiosity.
quests.textToSpeak: My neighbor gets a package every Monday, and it's always the same long box. What could be in it?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker says about the TV.
quests.explanation: Having a TV on without watching it, and nothing to do, shows boredom.
quests.textToSpeak: I finished my homework an hour ago. The TV is on, but I'm not really watching. There's nothing to do.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the plans and how the speaker sums them up.
quests.explanation: Pizza, a movie and calling it the best Friday ever show simple happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: Mom just said we can have pizza for dinner, and then a movie. Best Friday ever.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice which word the speaker uses to judge what happened.
quests.explanation: The speaker sees the situation as unfair and someone else got credit. Anger is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher gave my drawing to another student, and now it's on the wall with their name. It's not fair!

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what the speaker is remembering as they walk past.
quests.explanation: The speaker misses the old friends and the old times. That's what the clues add up to: sadness.
quests.textToSpeak: I walked past the empty house where my old friends lived. There's a new family there now.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to how the speaker prepares in the last seconds.
quests.explanation: Coaching themselves to breathe and smile just before a big moment shows nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: The interviewer is coming out of the room now. Okay. Deep breath. Smile. Deep breath.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the details the speaker has already planned.
quests.explanation: Planning even the snacks a day ahead shows eager anticipation. Everything points to excitement.
quests.textToSpeak: Tomorrow we're taking the train to the mountains! I already know which snacks I'm bringing.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker just learned about the other person.
quests.explanation: This is a fact the speaker didn't know, and they react with repeated questions. So surprised is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: You speak Spanish? To that man? I never knew you could speak Spanish!

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker decides to do.
quests.explanation: Moving closer to find out a secret shows curiosity.
quests.textToSpeak: She's whispering something to him and smiling. What are they planning? Let me get closer.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker is trying to hide.
quests.explanation: Trying not to yawn while listening to a long explanation shows boredom.
quests.textToSpeak: Grandpa is explaining his stamp collection again. I'm trying not to yawn. There are so many stamps.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about why someone reads the same letter three times.
quests.explanation: Rereading a warm letter shows how much it pleased them. So happy is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: I got a letter from my pen pal today, and she sent a photo of her new puppy. I read it three times!

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the question at the end and who it is aimed at.
quests.explanation: The repeated request and the sharp question show the speaker is upset with the person. Everything points to anger.
quests.textToSpeak: You left the door open again, and now the cat is outside. How many times do I have to ask you?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker says they could do right there.
quests.explanation: A very early start and a long day make the speaker say they could sleep at the desk. That's why tired fits best.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been up since five, and I still have two hours of work left. I could fall asleep right here on my desk.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker asks the other person to do.
quests.explanation: Asking to turn off the light and stay quiet shows the speaker wants to hide from danger. Fear is the natural reading.
quests.textToSpeak: Did you hear that? Something is moving in the garage. Turn off the light. Please stay quiet.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the two facts that make the speaker uneasy.
quests.explanation: The person is late and unreachable, so the speaker fears something is wrong. Everything points to worry.
quests.textToSpeak: It's midnight, and she's not home yet. She said nine, and now her phone is off.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen for how many different answers the speaker mentions.
quests.explanation: The speaker has three conflicting pieces of information and can't make sense of them. That's confusion.
quests.textToSpeak: Wait, so the meeting's at three, but the email says four, and Ben says it's tomorrow?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice who made the cake, and how other people reacted.
quests.explanation: The speaker did something new alone and people praised it. That's what the clues add up to: pride.
quests.textToSpeak: I made this whole cake by myself. My first cake ever, and everyone asked for a second piece.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to how fast the speaker's search becomes urgent.
quests.explanation: Losing a passport in a strange place makes the speaker panic. That's fear.
quests.textToSpeak: I turned around and my bag was gone. My passport was in it! I looked under the seat, in the aisle... nothing!

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker looks forward to, and what they leave out.
quests.explanation: Welcoming a peaceful day off with relief from work shows simple happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: Finally, the weekend. No alarm clock, no emails. Just me, my couch, and a long, quiet day.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Compare how the speaker was treated with how others were treated.
quests.explanation: The speaker was ignored while later customers were served, which feels unfair. That's why angry fits best.
quests.textToSpeak: I asked the waiter for water three times. Now the couple who arrived after us has their food.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the physical description and what the speaker wants next.
quests.explanation: Heavy legs and a wish to lie down after a long day show tiredness.
quests.textToSpeak: I ran six miles this morning and then worked all day. My legs feel like stone. I just want to lie down.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker hopes will not happen.
quests.explanation: Hoping not to be picked, in front of others, shows nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: Everyone else knows the answer, and I don't. I hope she doesn't call my name.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker has been doing all week.
quests.explanation: Smiling all week while preparing shows looking forward to it. That's excitement, not worry.
quests.textToSpeak: Tomorrow I start my new job. My clothes are ready, and I've been smiling about it all week.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what the new dress means now that the plan has changed.
quests.explanation: The plan is gone and the dress was bought for it. The speaker feels sadness about the lost event.
quests.textToSpeak: The tickets are sold out, so we can't go. And I already bought a new dress for it.
